patch.value:
**Version:** 2026.10.23 (global npm install).

Read-only commands write to the tracker when `schema/workflows.json` is missing: they recreate the file before (or while) serving the read. A tracker that an agent opens only to inspect — a read-only mount, a snapshot under review, a scratch rehearsal that must prove the source is untouched — is mutated by `pm list`.

### Reproduction

```bash
mkdir wf && cd wf
pm init --defaults
pm create --type Task --title x
rm .agents/pm/schema/workflows.json
pm list --limit 1        # or: get <id>, context --limit 1, search x --limit 1
ls .agents/pm/schema/    # workflows.json is back
```

Measured on 2026.10.23: `pm list`, `pm get` (even for a missing id), `pm context` and `pm search` each recreate the file; `pm --version` does not. The same write happens through the SDK when an extension command runs against the active tracker, so an extension cannot check isolation before the host has already written (found while reviewing a migration-rehearsal extension that must report `source_unchanged`).

### Expected

Read paths never write. A missing optional schema file resolves to the built-in defaults in memory, optionally with a warning (`schema_file_missing`, remedy `pm schema init` / `pm health --fix`). Materialising defaults stays an explicit mutation (`pm init`, `pm health --fix`, or the first real write), and a read-only filesystem keeps working for reads.

Related, closed: #265 (unknown schema subcommand mutated types.json), #1392 (read-only extension manage rewrote a tracked file), #928 (health read-only).
GH-1568: keep read-only commands from recreating missing workflow schema files
External report: https://github.com/unbraind/pm-cli/issues/1568. Revalidate the reported 2026.10.23 behavior against the checkout before implementation.

Reproduce missing workflows.json with list/get/context/search; keep reads free of persistent schema writes; retain explicit initialization and mutation repairs; prove file bytes and absence through public SDK and CLI
